title: Build or Pipeline Timeout in Globex CI/CD
text:
Symptom: Globex CI pipeline (Jenkins/GitLab CI) reports 'Pipeline exceeded maximum duration of 60 minutes', 'Stage timed out after 30m', or build agent is terminated mid-run. Artifact is not produced; deployment does not proceed.

Root Cause: Integration test suite awaiting real external service (Kafka, database) that is unavailable in CI; large Docker image build without layer caching; Globex data migration script processing unexpectedly large dataset; network-dependent step waiting on a connection that never arrives.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check Jenkins/GitLab build log for the last output line before timeout — this is where execution stalled
2. Look for lines like 'Waiting for connection...' or test names that never output a result
3. Check if the build consumed full timeout (60m) or a stage limit
4. Run the failing step locally with 'time' prefix to get baseline duration

Fix:
- Mock external services in CI: set GLOBEX_TEST_MODE=integration_mock to use Testcontainers or WireMock
- Enable Docker BuildKit cache: add DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 and --cache-from to docker build commands
- Globex Jenkins: increase pipeline timeout in Jenkinsfile: options { timeout(time: 90, unit: 'MINUTES') }
- GitLab CI: set timeout in .gitlab-ci.yml: timeout: 90 minutes per job
- Fix stalled tests: add per-test timeout annotations (@pytest.mark.timeout(60) or jest.setTimeout(30000))
- For data migration: batch process with LIMIT/OFFSET and checkpoint resume

Prevention: Set explicit timeouts on all external calls; run long jobs as scheduled pipelines (not on every commit); use Globex pipeline analytics dashboard to track build time trends.
